tasks.title: Telegram unavailable state: recover automatically and never strand first-run setup
tasks.outcome: If Telegram is unavailable, Dyk keeps retrying and users can always go back to saved chats and tasks.
tasks.goal: Repair the repository-confirmed defects of netbka/Dyk#415 (read the full issue with gh issue view 415 --repo netbka/Dyk). In app/src/telegram-ui.js the 'unavailable' state stops polling: render() calls stop() for unavailable, refresh() stops polling on any failure, and visibilitychange and the initial bootstrap refresh only AUTH states. So the promised automatic recovery never happens and the user cannot leave the panel. Make recovery real with bounded backoff polling and refresh on return to the page, give the user a working way back to saved chats and tasks, and apply the client-side optional leading '+' for phone numbers that #413 added only on the server. Do not touch production, the Telegram worker or live accounts.
constraints: Preserve rate limits and never issue unbounded provider requests while recovering.
acceptance: Focused regression tests fail on current main and pass with the fix: unavailable keeps bounded recovery polling, a later healthy status leaves the unavailable panel, returning to the page triggers a refresh, and the user can navigate back out.
A phone number without a leading '+' is accepted by the client and normalised as the server already does.
Dyk's required checks for the touched files pass, with exact commands and results in the report; any part needing a live device or production is listed as remaining, not claimed.
